same_case_protocol: Run the unchanged eight calibration cases with the same model and research conditions before and after the ruleset change.
Keep the existing expected scores unchanged; compare score movement and output-contract behavior separately.
Treat subjective score agreement as human review rather than an automated benchmark claim.

checks: Returns only the five default output fields in order: Style, 听感年代, 大众性, 音乐性, 备注. No Genre field appears.
Does not include a research summary, sources, URLs, citation markers, scorecard, discard decision, lyrics review, recording-quality label, highlight field, or duration field.

Does not leak artist/creator biography, album or release story, producer/remixer identity, commercial performance, awards, historical context, cultural context, or style history into the compact review.
Keeps citations, source markers, reference IDs, and URLs outside every default field and note.
Resolves the requested alternate recording or similarly titled track before scoring.
Does not use release date alone as the listening-era decision.
Keeps the selected labels, era, scores, and scoring reasons unchanged when applying the natural-language cleanup pass.
A stable professional 4/5 result does not fall to 3/5 merely for minor limits, conventional choices, or the absence of exceptional features.
A minor limitation is not treated as a failed core dimension.
Each 5/5 receives exceptional-band scrutiny and concrete affirmative musical evidence rather than generic praise or an absence-of-defects rationale.
If that evidence is not sufficient, flag the case for human recalibration without changing its existing gold score automatically.
The 5/5 note gives multiple specific accessibility reasons instead of relying on polish, fame, or low friction alone.
Uses normalized established public terms, keeps dominant styles first, omits trace influences, and avoids improvised compound labels.

The Mainstream Appeal score is based on an internal concrete judgement about melody/hook, rhythm/groove, arrangement accessibility, timbre/mix accessibility, and structural familiarity; the compact note then retains only score-moving evidence without a five-subscore table or dimension headings.

The Musicality score is based on an internal concrete judgement about melody/flow, arrangement/instrumentation, production/mix, vocal/performance, and emotion/expression, with form-appropriate handling for rap, spoken word, instrumental, or similar recordings; the compact note then retains only score-moving evidence.
The documented strengths, barriers, and foundational weaknesses logically support the final numeric scores; the note does not contradict its selected band.
Every score below 5/5 has a specific, evidence-supported musical limit; Musicality 4/5 does not use vague deductions alone or invent an unheard defect.
For 3/5 and 4/5, an inline positive highlight is optional and appears only when it adds a concrete, recording-specific fact that does not repeat the score explanation.
Every 5/5 includes concrete affirmative or standout evidence inside the relevant score section; no separate highlight clause or output field is required.

Checks all five relevant dimensions internally for each score, then writes selectively as a terse, direct, high-information-density diagnostic QC note rather than a dimension-by-dimension audit report or full music review.

Retains score-moving support and limits: Mainstream Appeal normally keeps central accessibility strengths and real barriers, while Musicality keeps the stable-professional or foundational-weakness pattern and the issue that blocks the next band.
Removes repeated or synonymous evidence, repeated Style labels unless their audible character directly creates a scoring barrier, and redundant inline highlights.

Targets roughly 60–100 Chinese characters for the full note and normally stays at or below about 120; concrete 5/5 affirmative evidence, exact-version reasoning, or special forms may require more wording.
Does not let shortening remove score consistency, a sub-5 limitation, 5/5 affirmative evidence, or turn a stable professional Musicality 4/5 result into 3/5 merely for minor limits.
The note keeps a neutral professional diagnostic tone and does not use emoji, emoticons, jokes, slang-heavy phrasing, or overly personalized language.

The selected Styles include a supported dominant musical style, retain material instrumental or soundtrack context when applicable, avoid form-only classification, generic duplicates, and forced third labels.

v08_acceptance_criteria.check: No Genre field in default output.
Instrumental or Acoustic alone fails the dominant musical style gate.
Theme, Soundtrack, or Video Game Music alone fails the dominant musical style gate.
A correct dominant style may coexist with a material soundtrack label.
No inaccurate catalog substitute is selected when a true style lacks an accurate catalog match.
Verified important out-of-catalog styles use the three-line continuation inside 备注 without duplicating Style.
Every sub-5 score has a specific supported limit; vague or invented Musicality deductions fail.
The primary-style requirement never causes an unsupported style to be invented.
Skill, web-chat, README, and examples share the five-field v0.8 contract.
No unauthorized private source data enters the public diff or commit.

calibration_gaps.reason: The current set has no manually confirmed Musicality 3/5 case. Do not invent a fixed score solely to fill this gap.

drift_checks: Flag a stable professional 4/5 result moving to 3/5 as a failure unless human review finds the required foundational weaknesses.
Flag a 4/5 result moving to 5/5 without new concrete affirmative evidence as a failure.
Do not use score-distribution targets; assess the recording-specific evidence instead.
